page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A2.Flex.16-128 is a general-purpose cloud instance configured with 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs running on the arm64 Ampere AmpereOne Ampere-1 platform at a fixed 3.0 GHz clock speed. Each vCPU maps directly to a single physical execution core without simultaneous multithreading, ensuring predictable compute execution. The instance is configured with 128 GB of memory, equating to 4.0 GB per core. It is provisioned without local storage, requiring network-attached block volumes for persistent data, and does not include GPU acceleration. Networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Synthetic benchmark evaluations illustrate strong multi-threaded scaling offset by restrained single-core throughput. The instance achieves a stress-ng multi-core score of 18279.21 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 244.0 GB/sec, placing it in the upper quartile for parallel data decompression. Conversely, single-threaded metrics reflect the lower instruction throughput typical of efficient Arm cores, registering 572.39 in single-core stress-ng and 1050.0 in Geekbench single-core tests. Memory subsystem evaluations record uncached sequential read bandwidth of 154.51 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 63.53 GB/sec, while cached read operations reach 2808.13 GB/sec.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the dedicated single-thread-per-core design offers high core density and consistent multi-threaded compute without the resource contention associated with hyperthreaded architectures. The absence of integrated NVMe or local disk drives places primary IO dependencies on remote block storage, which must be considered in IO-intensive designs. The instance delivers stable throughput for horizontal workloads, showing solid results in Redis operations at 42.46 million operations per second and static web serving throughput of 37.98 GB/sec. It is best suited for horizontally scaled microservices, multi-threaded batch data processing, web serving layers, and general-purpose Linux enterprise workloads.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A2.Flex.16-128 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the arm64 architecture, featuring 32 physical cores and 32 vCPUs from the Ampere AmpereOne Ampere-1 processor family clocked at 3.0 GHz. Operating with one thread per core, the instance provides dedicated compute resources alongside 128 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio. The instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address, contains no bundled local storage, and includes no GPUs. Benchmark metrics reveal moderate overall computing capability with average multi-threaded performance, demonstrated by 18279.21 in stress-ng multi-core and 244.0 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. However, single-threaded throughput is comparatively limited, reflected in lower single-core Geekbench and stress-ng scores. Memory read bandwidth reaches 154.51 GB/sec on uncached blocks. This hardware configuration is well aligned with parallelized backend workloads, static web serving, containerized services, and distributed database nodes that scale horizontally across physical cores.
